description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—on the TriviaQA dataset, as reported in the paper “Feedback Friction: LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback.” The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans a linear scale from approximately 0.71 to 1.00, with tick marks at intervals of roughly 0.02. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in linear increments of 0.2. The blue solid line with circle markers represents “Final Accuracy,” which begins at ~0.90 at 0.71 confidence, dips to ~0.73 at 0.73, rises to a peak of 1.0 at 0.79, and then fluctuates between ~0.88 and 1.0 for higher confidence values. The green dashed line with square markers, labeled “Initial Accuracy,” starts at ~0.55 at 0.71, rises to ~0.90 at 0.79, then declines to ~0.45 at 0.87 before rebounding to ~0.90 at 1.00. The orange dashed line with diamond markers, labeled “Δ Accuracy” (change in accuracy), begins at ~0.35 at 0.71, drops sharply to near 0.0 at 0.73, rises to ~0.28 at 0.83, dips to ~0.05 at 0.87, peaks at ~0.42 at 0.92, and then declines to ~0.08 at 1.00. Error bars are present for all three lines, indicating variability in measurements across data points.
